title: Candidate feedback draft - Ethan Hu (SWE Backend)
content:
Interviewers: Maya Thompson (hiring mgr), Alex Kim (tech lead), Priya Desai (peer)
Role: SWE - Backend (L4)
Date: 2026-03-03

Quick summary:
- Strong backend fundamentals, solid system design thinking. Comfortable with distributed systems concepts (consensus, sharding, caching).
- Implementation: clean and pragmatic; prefers simple, maintainable approaches.
- Some gaps around large-scale performance debugging and GPU inference pipeline specifics (not surprising).
- Great communicator, asks clarifying Qs early.

Scorecard (1-5)
- Technical (algorithms/data structures): 4
- System design: 4
- Product sense / tradeoffs: 4
- Coding (speed + correctness): 4 (minor off-by-one bug fixed quickly)
- Ownership / past impact: 4
- Culture fit / communication: 5
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire (4) - would pair well with infra/runtime team for backend services

Strengths:
- Focuses on operational simplicity: good at prioritizing correctness and observability over micro-optimizations.
- Experienced with microservices, metrics, and incident response; gave concrete examples from previous role scaling a request pipeline from 100s->10k RPS.
- Clear on testing strategies and CI practices.

Concerns / Risks:
- Limited exposure to ML inference-specific optimizations (quantization kernels, CUDA-level profiling). Would need ramp time working closely with serving-runtime team.
- Not deep C++ experience; mostly Go/Python/Java. For some infra components we rely on C++ expertise. Could be OK depending on team pairing.

Notes from interview rounds:
- System design: Asked to design a low-latency model inference proxy that routes requests to different model variants and caches prefix outputs. Candidate proposed a sharding strategy based on request signatures, discussed cache invalidation, and suggested async batcher for GPU utilization. Good tradeoff discussion between latency and throughput.
- Coding: Implemented a simplified LRU cache and a request deduping helper. Code was clear; picked appropriate data structures. Missed one concurrency edge-case (racy counter) but fixed after hint.
- Behavioral: Strong examples of taking ownership (led migration to k8s and wrote SLOs+runbooks). Comfortable with on-call rotation and postmortems.

Suggested next steps / team fit:
- Recommend moving forward to final manager loop / compensation conversation.
- Suggested pairing with serving-runtime engineers for a 2-4 week onboarding plan focusing on GPU inference pipeline and C++ codebase overview.

Open questions to resolve in follow-up:
- Confirm depth of low-level performance debugging experience (profilers, perf, nvprof / Nsight).
- Verify any past exposure to CUDA or C++ modules in production - candidate mentioned a C++ utility but unclear on scope.
- Compensation expectations and notice period (asked but not finalized).

Action items (for hiring team):
- Schedule manager loop with Lina Park (hiring director) and a senior serving-runtime engineer (Ben Ortiz).
- Recruiter to confirm compensation/notice details and get references.
- Prepare a 30/60/90 ramp outline if we proceed.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Likes observability: made multiple suggestions about per-route latency histograms and token-level tracing for LLM pipelines — aligns well with Redwood Console priorities.
- Would push back on excessive kernel-level micro-optimizations unless measurable ROI. Good cultural fit for pragmatic engineering.

End of draft.

(Will tidy and formalize for candidate-feedback thread after manager loop.)
